whatItIs.text: Sweet green peas picked young and frozen within hours of shelling, which locks in the sweetness that fresh pods lose within days.

historyNote.text: Peas are native to the Mediterranean and southwest Asia; dried peas were medieval staples of pease porridge and pea soup, while eating them fresh and green was an early-modern European luxury.

howToChoose.text: Shake the bag: free-flowing peas mean they were not thawed and refrozen; choose brands with short ingredient lists (peas, nothing else).

storage.text: Keep in the freezer; there is no need to thaw before cooking. The rulebook covers refreezing and leftovers.
storage.note: freezer guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: A handful of peas lifts fried rice, soup, or mashed potato; blitz the last of the bag into a bright soup with mint and stock.

substitutions.note: fresh are sweeter in season; canned are softer, add at the end
